description: Sun City West and Corte Bella are age-restricted communities in unincorporated Maricopa County. Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, covers rec centers, golf and roads.
summary: Sun City West is an unincorporated, age-restricted Del Webb community in Maricopa County, built from 1978 to 1997, between US-60 (Grand Avenue) and Loop 303. It has four recreation centers and seven golf courses. Neighboring Corte Bella is a gated 55+ golf community. Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, works with buyers and sellers in both.

sections.html:
After the original Sun City filled up, Del Webb started again a few miles west. Construction of Sun City West ran from 1978 to 1997 on an 11,000-acre site that included part of the old Lizard Acres cattle ranch, with Del Webb executive R.H. Johnson overseeing the work. The finished community holds roughly 16,900 homes.

Like its older neighbor, Sun City West has no city government. It is an unincorporated community and census-designated place in Maricopa County. Two groups shape daily life: the Recreation Centers of Sun City West, which owns and runs the amenities, and the Property Owners and Residents Association (PORA), which advocates for the community on county and state issues.

sections.h2: Rec centers, golf and the Sundome
sections.html:
The four recreation centers are Beardsley, Kuentz, Palm Ridge and R.H. Johnson. Between them you will find pools, fitness areas, hobby and craft studios, a library and a sports pavilion. The seven golf courses are Deer Valley, Grandview, Pebblebrook, Trail Ridge, Desert Trails, Echo Mesa and Stardust.

The Sundome Center for the Performing Arts is also in Sun City West, and it draws audiences from neighboring cities such as El Mirage. Lake Pleasant Regional Park is a drive to the northeast.

Corte Bella is a separate, gated 55+ community with a Sun City West mailing address. Del Webb and Pulte built its homes mostly in the 2000s. Its center is the 18-hole Corte Bella Golf Club, which operates on a membership basis separate from the homeowners association. Other amenities include a fitness center and spa, a social hall, a resort-style pool with a separate lap pool, tennis, pickleball and bocce courts, and an on-site restaurant.

Corte Bella is not part of the Recreation Centers of Sun City West, so its fees, rules and amenity access are different. Buyers comparing the two should request both sets of documents.

Sun City West and Corte Bella are both age-restricted communities. Sun City West operates under a Maricopa County senior overlay and its own deed restrictions, and Corte Bella has its own 55+ rules. Federal law allows 55+ housing when at least 80 percent of homes have a resident who is 55 or older, and the county overlay also limits long-term stays by younger residents. Specific requirements are set by each community's documents, so read them before you sign anything. Teigh's 55+ buying guide walks through the questions to ask.

Because the community was built over two decades, Sun City West homes show how Del Webb's designs changed from the late 1970s through the 1990s. Almost every home is single-level. Common types include:

  • Detached homes, including many that back onto one of the seven golf courses
  • Attached homes that share a wall
  • Condominiums

Floor plans, lot sizes and finishes differ from one phase to the next, so two homes built ten years apart can feel quite different inside. Corte Bella's homes came later, mostly in the 2000s. When you tour, ask the listing agent for the year built and any major updates, and compare homes from similar phases.

• Recreation center fees. Get the current Recreation Centers of Sun City West fee schedule, including anything owed at closing, and find out what each card or membership includes.
  • Corte Bella HOA and golf. HOA dues and Corte Bella Golf Club membership are separate. Ask for both.
  • Home age and systems. Homes from the 1970s and 1980s may need roof, AC, plumbing or electrical updates. A full inspection and a sewer scope are worth it.
  • Golf course lots. Look at the view, the orientation and the distance from tee boxes and cart paths.
  • Solar. Confirm whether any solar system is owned or leased.
  • Utilities. Electricity comes from APS, natural gas from Southwest Gas, and water and sewer from EPCOR.

Teigh's buyer services include reviewing these documents with you.

US-60 (Grand Avenue) runs along the southwest edge of Sun City West, and Loop 303 bounds it to the north and northwest. R.H. Johnson Boulevard is the main internal route, and Bell Road connects east toward Surprise, Sun City and Loop 101. Downtown Phoenix is about 23 miles to the southeast.

Most of Sun City West is not in any school district. Some parts fall within Dysart Unified School District and Peoria Unified School District. If school assignment matters for a specific property, check with the county and those districts.

sections.h2: Selling in Sun City West or Corte Bella
sections.html:
Buyers in both communities want to know about the roof, AC, water heater, updates, golf course position, and the fees they will owe. Be ready with your most recent fee statements, any HOA or rec center paperwork, and receipts for work done.

Many sellers are downsizing after years in the same home, and the job of sorting, packing and getting rooms photo-ready can feel big. Teigh helps with a staging plan, hands-on arranging with your own furniture, or full staging for vacant homes. Visit the home staging page for details. She prices every listing with a comparative market analysis rather than area averages.

faqs.a: Yes. Sun City West is an age-restricted active adult community that operates under a Maricopa County senior overlay and its own deed restrictions. Federal law allows 55+ communities when at least 80 percent of homes have a qualifying resident. Review the current rules before you buy, especially if a younger person will live in the home.

faqs.q: Is Corte Bella part of Sun City West?
faqs.a: Not exactly. Corte Bella shares a Sun City West mailing address, but it is a separate gated 55+ community built by Del Webb and Pulte, with its own HOA and amenities. It is not part of the Recreation Centers of Sun City West, and the Corte Bella Golf Club runs on a separate membership.

faqs.q: Is Sun City West a city?
faqs.a: No. Sun City West is an unincorporated community and census-designated place in Maricopa County, with no city government. The county handles zoning and roads, the Recreation Centers of Sun City West runs the amenities, and the Property Owners and Residents Association advocates for the community.

faqs.q: What are the recreation centers in Sun City West?
faqs.a: There are four: Beardsley, Kuentz, Palm Ridge and R.H. Johnson. They are run by the Recreation Centers of Sun City West, which also operates seven golf courses: Deer Valley, Grandview, Pebblebrook, Trail Ridge, Desert Trails, Echo Mesa and Stardust.

faqs.q: When was Sun City West built?
faqs.a: Del Webb built Sun City West from 1978 to 1997 on an 11,000-acre site west of the original Sun City. The community holds roughly 16,900 homes, most of them single-level. Corte Bella, next door, was built later, mostly in the 2000s.

faqs.q: Who provides utilities in Sun City West?
faqs.a: Arizona Public Service (APS) supplies electricity, Southwest Gas supplies natural gas, and EPCOR provides water and sewer service. Trash pickup is handled by a private hauler. Confirm the account setup for the specific home during escrow so service transfers smoothly on closing day.

faqs.q: Which freeways are near Sun City West?
faqs.a: Loop 303 runs along the north and northwest edges of Sun City West, and US-60 (Grand Avenue) runs along the southwest edge. R.H. Johnson Boulevard is the main road through the community, and Bell Road heads east to Surprise, Sun City and Loop 101.

faqs.q: Is Sun City West in a school district?
faqs.a: Mostly not. Most of Sun City West is outside any school district, while some parts are in Dysart Unified and Peoria Unified school districts. If school boundaries matter for a particular property, confirm with the county and the districts directly.
